habitat: Hedges and dry scrub forests; found up to an altitude of 1,300 m
ecological_importance: Acts as an important browse-resistant hedge plant, providing microhabitat and refuge for small insects and reptiles. Natural deterrent against herbivores.
threats: Overharvesting of wild populations for traditional pharmaceutical extraction.
field_identification_notes: Opposite, lanceolate leaves with a strong, pungent, medicinal aroma when crushed.
White bilabiate flowers marked with purple dots on spikes.
Woody, branching shrub habit found along hedges and dry scrub forests.
ml_relevance: Decussate elliptic-lanceolate leaves and dense terminal white spikes.

ar_information.quick_identification: Opposite lanceolate leaves with strong pungent smell; white flowers with purple dots.
ar_information.ecological_importance: Resilient shrub; natural herbivore deterrent; supports specialized pollinators.
ar_information.conservation_message: Secure / Least Concern. Used for millennia in Ayurveda as a premier expectorant and respiratory tonic.

vit_campus_relevance.location: Campus medicinal plant garden and landscaping hedges
